answer: At the drill site the crew cuts ice cores at marked depths and seals each sample in the station freezer, and only a core with a sealed record earns a seat. A signal core bought from another expedition fails the freezer: at the nebula of the sample the depth rings must match the drill log, and a bought core rings wrong. Forging the record means drilling for two winters, faking 180 core logs and paying 19,400, while the haven label on each tube is read at every thaw, so a core whose depth was never drilled is thrown out.
